name: The Folio Margin
prompt: Use case: ui-mockup. Asset type: high-fidelity desktop web-app composition comp for the existing Pattern/Like Today surface. Input image: the attached screenshot is the edit target and source of truth for the shell, palette, typography, content, and component character. Primary request: create compositional option B, The Folio Margin. Preserve the fixed left navigation and the Pattern/Like Private Observatory visual world exactly: warm drafting-paper grid, Observatory Green serif, compact sans-serif/mono labels, sparse Signal Coral, square geometry, fine rules, flat structural depth, no shadows. Recompose only the Today main canvas into a measured editorial folio that makes the PRIMARY THEME the first-viewport focal point. Structure in order: a narrow internal folio margin immediately inside the main canvas holds the eyebrow TODAY / DAILY CHAPTER, a vertically stacked or compact date Sunday, August 9, and the three real metadata chips. A fine vertical rule separates this folio margin from the reading. To its right, begin immediately with the exact primary-theme text Steady pressure asks for a smaller, firmer commitment than the one you had in mind. in dominant large serif type. Continue below in one reading column with supporting influence, cycle phase, timing, italic reflection, then restrained uncertainty and context annotations treated as marginal footnotes rather than cards. Why this reading? closes the same column as a square footnote disclosure. Show enough of the complete page to prove the structure; the hierarchy should feel like a private annotated folio, not a dashboard. Constraints: change only hierarchy and composition inside the Today main canvas; preserve all real copy shown in the screenshot where legible; no new actions, no journaling, no Timing link, no rounded corners, no pills, no gradients, no cosmic imagery, no invented data, no drop shadows, no multi-card grid. This must read as a designed responsive web UI comp, never as a poster or room scene.
